drafts.title: Editing is not the bottleneck. Selection is.
drafts.thesis: The highest-leverage content system improves the decision about what to cut before it tries to make edits faster.
drafts.audience_job: Help builders with an archive of conversations, calls, or ideas choose a clip with enough context to stand alone.

claims.text: A clip can fail even when the edit is polished, because the selected moment lacks enough context to stand on its own.
A useful candidate moment contains tension, proof, and a payoff a viewer can understand without the full recording.

drafts.draft_body:
HOOK
Most content teams think repurposing starts in the edit. It starts earlier: with selection.

BODY
If every minute of a recording gets the same chance, you are not choosing a story. You are scanning for noise.

Before I cut anything, I look for four signals: the context is intact; there is real tension; a piece of proof appears; and the payoff changes an operating decision.

That gives an editor something worth sharpening. It also means a short clip can stand alone without pretending the original conversation never existed.

CLOSE
The next content system I am building is not an auto-publisher. It is a selection layer for owned material: transcript, candidate moments, human ranking, then a clear edit brief.

COMPANION POST
Fast editing is useful. Choosing the wrong moment faster is not.

For any long-form recording, identify the passages where context survives the cut, tension is clear, proof arrives, and the payoff is useful. Then let a human choose what deserves production.

That is the difference between a content factory and an editorial system.
drafts.accessibility: Captions required for video; companion text provides the full argument; no visual-only claim is required.
drafts.rights: Original copy. Reference workflow only; no creator wording, footage, audio, or visual treatment is reused.
drafts.next_human_move: Record one 45–60 second first take, then add an owned transcript before any edit decision.

drafts.title: A hook is a mechanism, not a sentence to steal.
drafts.thesis: Original work comes from understanding why attention holds, then translating the mechanism into a truthful brand-specific promise.
drafts.audience_job: Help operators use reference material without turning their content system into a plagiarism machine.

claims.text: Reference material can be useful for analyzing attention mechanisms without copying the expression that carried them.
Specificity, contrast, proof, identity, and curiosity are useful categories for a human hook review.

drafts.draft_body:
OPEN
Do not save hooks so you can rewrite them. Save them so you can understand the job they are doing.

FRAME
A strong opening usually earns attention through one mechanism: specificity, contrast, proof, identity, or curiosity. The words are not the asset. The mechanism is.

EXAMPLE
Instead of borrowing someone else’s line, ask: what proof would make this true for my audience? What contrast does my experience actually earn? What question can I answer with a real system, not a tease?

CLOSE
That produces original content with a clearer point of view—and it gives your future self a library of thinking, not a folder of borrowed sentences.

CAROUSEL OUTLINE
1. A hook is a mechanism, not a sentence.
2. Capture the context, not just the words.
3. Classify the mechanism.
4. Translate it through a truth your brand can prove.
5. Keep the reference boundary visible.
drafts.accessibility: Use full on-screen text in the caption; every carousel panel needs equivalent body copy and descriptive alt text.
drafts.rights: Original copy. All external examples stay at mechanism level with URLs and a reference-only rights state.

drafts.title: Build an editorial system before you build an automation system.
drafts.thesis: A responsible AI content workflow preserves human judgment at source selection, evidence review, authorship, and release.
drafts.audience_job: Give creators a teachable model for using AI without giving up judgment or inventing performance claims.

claims.text: Automation can accelerate a weak editorial decision as easily as a strong one.
Human decision points should remain explicit at source selection, claim review, authoring, and release.

drafts.draft_body:
LESSON PROMISE
AI can accelerate production without becoming the editor-in-chief.

THE MODEL
1. Collect source material with provenance.
2. Choose one opportunity a human actually wants to pursue.
3. Generate a structured draft, not a finished claim.
4. Review source rights, accessibility, brand voice, and evidence.
5. Publish only after a human approves the final version.

WHY THIS MATTERS
The goal is not to make more posts. It is to reduce the distance between a real idea and a clear, useful artifact—without hiding who made the decisions.

EXERCISE
Take one owned recording. Identify one moment with context, tension, proof, and payoff. Draft a 45-second explanation. Mark every factual claim with its basis before you edit the first frame.
